final_diagnosis: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I'm here because for the last two years and three months, I've been experiencing an overwhelming amount of energy and an unusually elevated, happy mood. I also barely need any sleep anymore but still feel completely refreshed and ready to go. It's been going on for so long that I figured I should finally talk to someone about it.

Have you ever had hallucinations or strongly fixed beliefs that others said weren’t true during times when your mood was not unusually high or energized? If so, did those symptoms last for at least 2 weeks on their own?
No, I haven't experienced any hallucinations or those kinds of beliefs when my mood was normal or low. Those feelings of being special only seem to happen during the times when I am highly energized.
When you feel highly energized, do you ever hear or see things others don’t, or have beliefs like having special powers or an important mission that others say aren’t true?
I do strongly believe that I am a very special person with an important mission to fulfill in this world. However, I don't hear or see things that other people can't.
Do other people tell you this special mission isn’t true or realistic, and do you still feel completely certain about it anyway?

Yes, people around me constantly tell me it's unrealistic, but they simply don't have the vision to understand it. I am absolutely certain of my purpose, and their doubts don't shake my confidence at all because I know what I am meant to achieve!
During these energized periods, has this led to major problems like being hospitalized, getting into serious trouble, or being unable to function at work, school, or home?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about whether it has caused any major problems or serious trouble for me. I just feel like I am doing what I am supposed to be doing.

Have your beliefs about this mission caused clear consequences, like spending large amounts of money, quitting jobs or school, damaging relationships, or others becoming so worried they tried to get you emergency help?
No, I haven't really experienced those kinds of consequences with my job or money. People might get worried, but no one has ever gone as far as trying to get me emergency help.
Even without those consequences, have these beliefs ever made it hard for you to do your work or school tasks, take care of yourself, or get along with people at home?

Yes, because I feel so capable, I often take on far too many projects at once at work, which can get chaotic and overwhelming. My mood also shifts quickly, and I get very irritated with people at home when they don't understand my vision. This definitely causes some friction and makes it hard to manage everything smoothly.
Do you believe your special mission gives you abilities or powers that other people do not have, or is it more a strong sense of purpose without special powers?

I absolutely believe I possess superior talents and abilities that set me apart from everyone else. My intellect and capabilities are on a completely different level, which is exactly why I am the only one who can fulfill this mission.
Do you mean you feel unusually confident and talented, or do you believe you truly have special powers or abilities beyond what is realistically possible?

I definitely feel an extraordinary amount of confidence, and my talents are vastly superior to what they used to be. At the same time, I truly believe I have a unique, special mission in life that others find hard to believe or accept as possible.

Do you believe you can do things that are actually impossible for other people, like having supernatural powers, receiving special messages, or being chosen in a way that cannot be explained realistically?

Yes, I truly believe I have been chosen in a unique way that goes beyond what most people can realistically understand. My superior abilities allow me to achieve things that others find completely impossible, which is why this mission is mine alone.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a prolonged period of abnormally elevated mood and increased energy with markedly decreased need for sleep, along with grandiosity and clear psychotic content (fixed beliefs of being specially chosen and able to do impossible things). The psychotic symptoms occur only during the elevated mood state and not for at least 2 weeks outside of it, supporting Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features rather than a primary psychotic disorder. Functional impairment is present through work chaos and interpersonal conflict.
